ai.description: *Raorchestes aureus* is a small shrub frog (approx. 20 mm) with a golden-yellow dorsum. It is distinguished by a dark brown lateral stripe and prominent, translucent, reddish-orange webbing on the feet.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes aureus* is uniquely distinguished from similar congeners by its vibrant, uniform golden-yellow dorsal coloration, which lacks the distinct patterns or spots seen in others.
ai.habitat: *Raorchestes aureus* inhabits high-altitude evergreen forests and shola grasslands in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 1,500 and 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: *Raorchestes aureus* is primarily nocturnal, remaining active at night to forage for small invertebrates within the dense vegetation of its high-altitude forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes aureus* undergoes direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. They breed during the monsoon, laying small clutches of eggs in arboreal microhabitats.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Raorchestes aureus* is endemic to the high-altitude shola-grassland mosaics of the southern Western Ghats in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, typically above 1,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Raorchestes aureus* consists of a series of high-pitched, metallic "tink" notes, typically heard from the canopy of evergreen forests.
